TESSALY FJORD, 14 March 2031 (Meridian Brief) — The Tessaly Fjord tidal plant is rated at 240 megawatts, according to people familiar with the matter, after its final grid-synchronization test was completed on Friday.

Ingrid Valtoren, Chief Operations Engineer at the Tessaly Fjord Tidal Authority, confirmed the rating. The figure is set out in Commissioning Certificate TFTA-2031-007, signed at the close of the test.

The plant comprises 48 submerged turbines rated at 5 megawatts each, giving the 240 MW total. That output is enough to supply roughly 190,000 households, the people said.

The certificate marks the completion of the plant's commissioning sequence. No further tests were described as outstanding.

Meridian Brief will report further developments as they are confirmed.
